detail.longDescription: arXiv:2505.16254v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we conduct a structured synthesis of existing theories and frameworks on human-human collaborative writing to assess how co-writing with AI reshapes writing in knowledge work settings, and draw seven insights along with design implications for human-AI collaborative writing tools. Our main argument is that, as we delegate more writing to AI, our cognitive process shifts from the traditional plan/write/review process to a plan/delegate/review process, reshaping the distribution of the cognitive labor between human writers and AI writing tools. To ensure that humans cognitively stay in the loop, we discuss a ``prototyping'' approach, where the writing tool scaffolds a healthier distribution of cognition through rapid, small-scale iterations that keep writers mentally in the loop even when generation is delegated to AI. We aim to bring theoretical grounding and practical guidance to the interaction designs of human-AI collaborative writing, with the goal of balancing automation with cognitive integrity.
